text:
Maya: quick heads-up — saw a fragmentation spike on host-pool-3 during the 03:10-05:30 UTC window. p99 token latency nudged up ~18% on small-batch traffic. Thinking out loud: add an 'ageing_budget' heuristic that prefers compacting slabs that haven't been touched in a while before we spend cycles prefetching.

Liam: can you paste the numbers? is this visible in tenant-level telemetry or global? :thinking_face:

Maya: tenant-level, mostly medium-tenants with mixed embed+chat workloads. example: tenant-42 resident-set delta +120MB, compactable slab bytes ~78MB, prefetches triggered ~230/s. p95 latency stable, p99 slipped.

Jamal: curious — do we have eviction churn metrics? compacting older slabs might increase CPU work and risk latency spikes if done inline.

Maya: yep, churn is low-ish today, but compaction happens opportunistically during non-critical windows. Proposal is to make it policy-driven: an ageing budget that limits bytes/sec for compaction and sets a prefetch backoff when budget is near-depleted.

Anya: that sounds sensible. tradeoffs: 1) slower warmups for new requests if we throttle prefetch; 2) if budget is too low, hot-slab fragmentation remains. what's the heuristic to pick slabs for compact vs prefetch?

Maya: simple ranking for prototype: score = (time_since_last_touch_sec / slab_size_mb) * hotness_penalty. prefer highest score for compaction. only compact slabs with score > threshold and when compaction_rate < ageing_budget.max_compact_bytes_per_sec.

Liam: can you show a quick config snippet? easier for reviewers to grok.

Maya: pasted below — this is the prototype config we'll wire into the allocator's policy layer:

```yaml
ageing_budget:
  enabled: true
  min_age_sec: 600         # don't compact slabs younger than this
  max_compact_bytes_per_sec: "64MB"
  prefetch_backoff_at_util: 0.75  # when resident_util > this, dial down prefetches
  score_threshold: 0.8
  sample_window_sec: 30
```

Jamal: +1 to the budget idea. only ask that compaction be async and rate-limited by CPU budget too (not just bytes/sec). we saw CPU-starve blips during earlier compaction runs.

Anya: also consider tenant-priority. dedicated customers should be allowed to opt-out of aggressive compaction if it impacts their latencies. maybe a per-tenant policy override.

Maya: agreed. plan: prototype the budget in allocator, make compaction async (worker pool with CPU tokens), wire a tenant override flag, and run a 2-week canary on staging with workloade replay.

Liam: what's the measurement plan? (specific metrics and thresholds)

Maya: will track: resident_set_delta, compact_bytes/sec, prefetch_rate, p99/p95 latency, CPU_steal and compaction_cpu_seconds. success criteria: resident_set fragmentation drop >= 30% and p99 not worsen by >5% for target tenants.

infra-bot: canary job queued: `canary/proto-ageing-budget` (id: canary-4821). will post run results to #eng-runtime-canary. :robot_face:

Maya: thanks — I'll open a brief RFC with the prototype design, config fields, and perf test plan. tagging @Liam @Jamal for review.

Liam: sounds good. :thumbsup:

Jamal: happy to review, will add compaction CPU-rate limits in comments.

Anya: thanks — if you want I can add a tenant opt-out patch for the console flags.

Maya: perfect. I'll drop the RFC link once it's up and attach the replay dataset.
